overview.text: Indian Overseas Bank invites IRDAI-licensed Stand-Alone Health Insurance companies for a corporate agency tie-up to distribute health insurance products to its customers through branches and digital channels. The arrangement is initially for 3 years, renewable at the Bank's discretion for a further 3 years. Reference RFP/SAHI/003/2026-27, dated 11.05.2026.

summary.issuing_organization: Indian Overseas Bank; Marketing & Development Department, 763 Anna Salai, Central Office, Chennai-600002; Ref. RFP/SAHI/003/2026-27; queries: mdd@iob.bank.in, 044-28519639/ 044-71729204

scope.text: Corporate agency arrangement with one or more additional Stand-Alone Health Insurance companies to distribute individual and group health insurance products through branches and digital channels including internet banking and mobile banking.
Customise insurance products for every segment of the Bank's customers, with premiums in tune with market rates and competitive.
Support the Bank on sales, renewals, claims, customer complaint resolution, MIS, training, IT and manpower across the country.
Provide day-to-day data on policies issued, renewals, lapses and claims, with real-time data exchange with the Bank, and give the Bank portal access through a User ID and password.
Source business from all centres for the initial 01 year; permission for the subsequent 2 years may be extended by the Bank on satisfactory performance, subject to annual review.
Provide MIS updates on status of customer complaints on a weekly/fortnightly/monthly basis.
Settle claims without delay and within IRDAI timelines, run a grievance redressal procedure, issue renewal notices well before expiry, and issue policy documents and endorsements without delay.
Annexure 16 information security scope applies if data is hosted on the successful bidder's own premises (data centre).

key_requirements.text: Bid must meet every minimum eligibility criterion in Annexure-1; a proposal failing any one is rejected straight away.
Bidder must sign the Pre-Contract Integrity Pact (Annexure-17); a bidder not signing or refusing to sign is disqualified.
Bid must be submitted only through the Bank's e-tendering portal using a Class III Digital Certificate with signing and encryption; email, fax, post or courier bids are rejected.
Successful bidder must not sub-contract any part of the services without the Bank's prior written consent.
Successful bidder must inform the Bank within 24 hours of any regulatory breach, penalty, show cause or warning issued by IRDAI, SEBI, RBI or other regulators.
Successful bidder must bear all expenditure on integration of APIs, technology or system synchronisation, and comply with all applicable IRDAI regulations and guidelines.
Successful bidder must keep Bank customer data confidential and not use or disclose it for any purpose other than services under this RFP and the Agreement.
Successful bidder must provide online system access for MIS and MIS reports on business under the contract, and maintain policyholder records in safe custody.
AI/ML models used by the bidder must not be trained on Bank or Bank customer sensitive data and must be deployed on-premises by default; cloud or third-party AI needs the Bank's prior approval.
Bank must be notified within 4 hours of any suspected data breach from discovery; vulnerability assessment at least half-yearly and penetration testing at least yearly.

eligibility.text: Must hold a valid IRDAI insurance licence, valid on the date of RFP submission; copy of original licence and current licence with proof of renewal required.

Must be a government organization/PSU or a company registered under the Companies Act 1956 /2013 and with IRDAI, in existence for at least 5 years in standalone health insurance with business in India in the last 5 years.

Must have at least 3 years of experience in Bancassurance and a corporate agency tie-up with at least 2 Scheduled Commercial Banks, preferably 1 Public Sector Bank; certificate from beneficiary bank required.
Must have a minimum Claim Settlement Ratio of 90% in the last 2 financial years as on 31.03.2025 (FY24-25 and FY23-24).
Must have a minimum Solvency Ratio of 150% as on 31.03.2025 (C.A. certificate basis).
Must have minimum average Rs.5000 Crores underwritten premium (new business plus renewal) in the last 2 years.
Must sign the Integrity Pact (Annexure-17), a preliminary qualification; in a joint venture all partners must sign.

Must confirm in Annexure 15 that it is not blacklisted by any tie-up partner, PSU, PSB or private bank, has no pending cheating/fraud case, and has no IRDAI or other regulatory penalty or warning (details to be given if any).

commercial_requirements.text: Successful bidder pays the Bank remuneration/commission on each policy issued at mutually decided rates, within IRDAI regulations, on a monthly basis.
Commission must be remitted to the Bank by the 10th working day of every month with details of all policies issued till the end of the previous month.

Annexure-4 asks for maximum commission approved by IRDAI and maximum offered to the Bank per product; all commission must comply with IRDAI (Expenses of Management, including Commission, of Insurers) Regulations, 2024 (effective 01.04.2024).
Bank reserves the right to negotiate pricing/commission with the L1 insurance company anytime during the tenure of the agreement.
Bank may impose penalties and Liquidated Damages if performance is not as per its satisfaction; rate or cap not specified in the document.
Bank may set off any amount due to the Company and is not liable to pay damages to the Company in any condition.
Bidder bears all bid preparation costs and the cost of registration on the e-tendering portal.
EMD/bid security and Performance Bank Guarantee are mentioned in the Integrity Pact but no amount is stated anywhere; tender fee and warranty are not specified in the document.

project_duration.text: Tie-up is initially for a period of 3 years, subject to satisfactory performance and annual review; the Bank may renew for a further 3 years or discontinue.
Business sourcing from all centres is permitted for the initial 01 year, then 2 years more on satisfactory performance, subject to annual review.
Tie-up commencement date is to be determined or advised after the selection process is complete.
Integrity Pact is valid for 5 years or until complete execution of the contract including warranty, whichever is later; if the bidder is unsuccessful it expires six months after contract signing.

important_conditions.text: Evaluation: three stages - minimum eligibility (any failure rejects the proposal), technical evaluation carrying 70 marks, and a presentation carrying 30 marks.

Evaluation: technical scoring covers 14 parameters, maximum 70 marks in total, including solvency ratio, profit after tax, claim settlement ratio, Gross Written Premium, bank tie-ups, branches and penalties.
Evaluation: top shortlisted bidders on technical score are invited to present; the Bank decides the cut-off marks and the number of bidders; bidders bear their own travel and stay costs.
Submission: only via the e-tendering portal https://iobtenders.auctiontiger.net; the portal accepts no bids after the deadline and the acknowledgement must be kept.
Submission: data must be in the formats of Annexure 1 to Annexure 20, in English, in Indian Rupees, for the financial year ending March 31, 2025; other formats make the proposal non-compliant.
Submission: every page of the RFP document must be signed by the authorised person; bids with unsigned documents will be summarily rejected.
Submission: no overwriting, erasures or handwritten corrections; replies such as OK, accepted or noted are not acceptable.
Submission: verify the Class III Digital Certificate with the service provider at least two days before the due date; a mock drill is advised.

Risk: submission mode conflicts. The schedule and bid process allow submission only through the e-tendering portal, but one preface bullet says the bid in physical form with supporting documents should be submitted by the due date.
Risk: indemnity is uncapped, covering all actions, claims, losses and advocates' fees from repudiation or delay in settlement of claims or any matter connected with the agreement.
Risk: penalties and Liquidated Damages can be imposed at the Bank's satisfaction with no rate or cap stated; the Bank is not liable to pay damages to the Company.

Risk: the Bank may terminate by notice without assigning reason and the Company cannot terminate for convenience, while another clause says either party may terminate the tie-up per IRDAI Regulations.
Risk: suspected data breaches must be notified within 4 hours, and the provider bears financial losses or penalties up to an 'agreed Cap' that the document does not define.
Risk: how the 70 technical and 30 presentation marks combine into a final rank is not stated, yet award goes to the L1 bidder with commission negotiable afterwards.

overview.text: Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), Central Office, Mumbai, invites online two-bid tenders for procurement and implementation of tools for the DPDP Act, 2023 and DPDP Rules, 2025, covering 12 modules such as consent management, data discovery and breach management, for a period of five (5) years. Ref: LIC-CO/ERM/CSD/RFP/2026-27/DPDPA_Tools Dated: 13/07/2026.

summary.issuing_organization: Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC); Central Office, ERM/CSD (Cyber Security) Department, Mumbai; Ref: LIC-CO/ERM/CSD/RFP/2026-27/DPDPA_Tools Dated: 13/07/2026; contact: dpdpbid@licindia.com

scope.text: Supply, implement and support a DPDP compliance solution of 12 modules: Data Privacy Notice Management, Consent Management Platform, Cookie Consent Management, Data Discovery & Mapping, Data Principal Rights Management (including Grievance Redressal), DPIA, ROPA, Personal Data Breach Management, Third Party Vendor Risk Management, Compliance Reporting & Dashboards, Workflow Management and a DPDP Program Management portal. List is not exhaustive.

Six phases with deliverables for each module: Planning & Designing workshop, Implementation, User acceptance testing, Movement to production, Training and knowledge transfer, and Post implementation support. The activity list is indicative, not exhaustive.
Supply and install software and hardware (if any) for DC and DR in HA mode, deployed in pre-production, production and DR environments, with all licences registered in LIC's name.

Integrate with LIC applications and systems including SIEM, PAM, Active Directory/LDAP, SMS and email gateways and a centralized identity repository; the solution should work with SOAR for incident handling.

Bidder must engage OEMs for plan, design and implementation; the OEM holds overall implementation responsibility, certifies the architecture and audits deployment at the end of implementation and once every year during the contract period.

After go-live, manage and monitor the solution end to end for the five-year term, with level-1, level-2 and level-3 support, root cause analysis, VAPT remediation, DR drill support and a 24/7/365 support contact centre.

Training at LIC premises in Mumbai: hands-on training before and after implementation, certification-level training for three participants at no additional cost, and training twice every year for each module till end of contract.
Deploy a total of 24 dedicated onsite resources for the contract duration, including an onsite Project Manager, on LIC premises in Mumbai.

key_requirements.text: The complete solution must be deployed on-premises only at LIC; no component may be deployed outside the LIC network at any time.
The solution must not go live until all VAPT observations are resolved and LIC's delegated committee approves; bidder is solely responsible for closing the findings.

Bidder must comply with every parameter of Annexure XV technical specifications (separate Excel); non-compliance to any parameter means the bid is not evaluated. The specifications are minimum, equivalent or higher may be quoted.
The bidder needs to provide hardware, support and licences for 5 years post Go-live for all modules; all licences must be in the name of Life Insurance Corporation of India.
The solution must accommodate a yearly project growth rate of up to 10%, with licence prices and a breakdown of charges for additional licences quoted upfront.
Software and accessories must be IPv6 compatible and prepared for TLS 1.3 or higher; encryption of data in transit and at rest is desirable.
A detailed execution plan with designs must be submitted to LIC within 5 weeks of placing the order; execution starts only after LIC approves it.
All onsite personnel must be full-time employees on the vendor's payroll; outsourced or subcontracted personnel are not permitted. Police background verification is required.
Desirable: RTO of 4 hours and RPO of 15 minutes; DC and DR in active-passive mode for all infrastructure.
Desirable: log storage of at least 12 months, and 2 years in the SIEM, with logs retrievable within 5 hours of any breach.

eligibility.text: Bidder must be a system integrator and a registered legal entity in India in operation for a minimum of 5 years preceding the RFP date, with valid GST registration and PAN card.

Bidder must have average annual turnover of not less than INR 100 Crores over the last three audited financial years (FY2023-2024, FY2024-2025, FY2025-2026), operating profit (EBITDA) in those years and positive net worth as on RFP date; CA certificate without riders.

Bidder or OEM must have implemented, or be implementing, privacy automation solutions with at least consent management, data principal rights management and data discovery for at least two (2) organizations in the insurance and/or banking sectors.

Bidder must have revenue of at least 50 Crore from DPDP related projects and Services / Cyber Security Projects in each of the last 3 financial years (FY 2023-24, FY 2024-25, FY 2025-26). Bidder and OEM must have a support center in Mumbai with 24x7 onsite, telephonic and remote support.

Bidder must have a minimum of 30 permanent Data Privacy / IT Security professionals on payroll with certifications such as CIPT, CIPP/E, CIPM, DSCI, CISSP, OSCP, CEH, CISA or CISM, and must hold any 3 of ISO27001, ISO9001, ISO22301, ISO 20000.

OEM must have average annual turnover of not less than INR 500 Crores over the last three audited financial years, with positive EBITDA, PAT and Net Worth in each; its product must be commercially available for a minimum of two years and implemented or under implementation at at least three enterprise customers.

OEM must have a dedicated implementation team (Project Manager, Solution Architect, Privacy Consultant, Technical Specialists) with minimum five years' experience. Bidder or OEM must have an in-house privacy legal team or a signed MoU with law firms or privacy consultancies, with at least two CVs of legal experts (LLB/LLM).

Bidder must not be blacklisted by Government of India, RBI, SEBI or IRDAI (void if a court stay order is obtained), and must give a duplicate-participation undertaking, a signed Integrity Pact, Manufacturer Authorization Form and Land Border declaration. Consortium bids are rejected.

commercial_requirements.text: Bid processing fee: non-refundable Rs.11,800/- inclusive of GST (10000+18%GST), paid online. Micro and Small Enterprises are exempt with an MSME/NSIC certificate. A bid without the fee or valid exemption documents is rejected.

EMD: INR 83,00,000 (Rupees Eighty-Three Lakhs Only) as an unconditional and irrevocable Bank Guarantee payable at Mumbai, valid for one year from the last date of submission; non-submission disqualifies. MSEs with MSME/NSIC certificate are exempt. Unsuccessful bidders get a refund within 45 days of the result.

Performance Bank Guarantee: unconditional and irrevocable, 5% of total Contract Value, due within 15 days of the selection letter and valid for 63 months. Delay costs Rs.5,000/- per day up to Rs.1,00,000/-; after 35 days LIC may cancel and award to the L2 bidder at L1 prices.

Prices in Indian Rupees, all-inclusive excluding GST, fixed for the entire contract period with no escalation or variation. Bidder must factor a maximum of 25% scope changes into the quoted cost and all costs of obtaining retrospective consent from Data Principals.

No advance payment; paid in INR by NEFT after deductions. Milestones per solution: 40 % on delivery of all software/appliances and contract signing; 40 % on installation, integration, initial OEM audit and acceptance testing, plus 100% of Direct Premium Support Cost with OEMs; 15 % after go-live and OEM validation; 5 % on training and documentation. Onsite services are paid quarterly in arrear subject to SLA.

SLA breach penalties are capped cumulatively at 10% of the contract value (TCO); delivery and installation penalties at 10% of the PO value; onsite and offsite support penalties at 100% of quarterly charges.

Delay penalties: 0.25 % of the total PO value of the hardware per week of delay or part thereof, same rate on delayed software/appliances value; HLD and LLD beyond 6 weeks of PO, 0.02% of the total PO value per week; onsite person leaving before 1 year, 2 % of annual on-site charges plus 1% per repeat.

Comprehensive on-site warranty of five (5) years from installation and acceptance, including updates and patches at no extra cost; spares and support must be available for a minimum of six years from installation.

project_duration.text: Total engagement of five (5) years, equivalent to sixty (60) months, from issuance of the Letter of Award (LoA), subject to extension at LIC's discretion.
The bidder shall complete the entire activity within 20 weeks of signing of contract.

Milestones from T (date of Letter of Award): Phase 1 Planning & Designing Workshop T+2 Weeks; Phase 2 Delivery of Hardware T + 8 Weeks; Phase 3 Implementation T+ 16 Weeks; Phase 4 User acceptance testing T+ 17 Weeks; Phase 5 Movement to production T+ 19 Weeks; Phase 6 Training and knowledge transfer T+20 Weeks.
Post Go-Live support runs 5 years from Go-live date.

Contract steps: submit receipt of Purchase Order within 7 days, PBG within 15 days and contract/SLA form within 30 days of being intimated; project commences within 7 days from Contract / SLA execution.
LIC may extend maintenance and support for up to additional two years (i.e. 6th and 7th year) at a mutually agreed rate; the contract may be renewed after 5 years at LIC's discretion.
On termination or expiry, knowledge transfer must not exceed 90 days and transition to a successor must not exceed six months.

important_conditions.text: Evaluation: Two-bid system. Bidders must meet all eligibility criteria, non-compliance means rejection, and only eligibility-qualified bidders' commercial bids are opened. No technical scoring or weights are specified in the document.

Evaluation: Qualified bidders go to an online reverse auction run by LIC's authorised e-procurement provider; the lowest total cost of ownership (TCO) is L1 and is the successful bidder. If only one bidder qualifies there is no auction and LIC may negotiate the price.

Evaluation: Future-year maintenance prices are discounted to net present value at a 10% rate. If more than five bidders qualify, the highest-priced (H1) bidder is eliminated from the auction if more than 40% above the average of quoted prices.

Evaluation: Qualified bidders must give a technical presentation. Clarifications sought by LIC not submitted within 5 working days make the bid liable to rejection. Arithmetic errors: unit price prevails over total, words over figures.

Submission: Bids are submitted online at www.tenderwizard.com/LIC using a Digital Signature Certificate, and hard copies in sealed envelopes must follow within three working days of eligibility bid opening. Consortium bids are rejected.

Submission: Separate sealed envelopes for eligibility bid and commercial bid, each with a read-only pen drive, inside a third outer envelope addressed to the Executive Director (ERM); bid fee, EMD and signed Integrity Pact go in a separate sealed envelope. Hard copies must be spirally bound, serially numbered, signed and stamped on every page.

Submission: Commercial bid in the Annexure-VIII Excel sheet, password protected by LIC and to be opened only in MS Excel; a password mismatch can lead to rejection and EMD forfeiture. Prices appear only in the commercial bid, in INR; prices in the eligibility bid may lead to rejection.

Submission: Required forms include Annexure-I covering letter, II company profile, III to V declarations, VI EMD bank guarantee, X MAF, XII land border declaration, XIV Integrity Pact and XV technical specifications, plus BoQ/BoM. Each violation of submission instructions costs Rs.5,000/- (cap Rs.10,000/-) from EMD.

Risk: Liability is both capped and unlimited. Aggregate liability is limited to the total Contract price plus DPDP Act penalties, yet vendor liability for misconduct, gross negligence, IPR infringement or confidentiality breach is unlimited, and the vendor must indemnify LIC for all Data Protection Board of India penalties.

Risk: Timeline reference is inconsistent. The entire activity must finish within 20 weeks of signing of contract, but milestones run from T, defined as the Letter of Award date, and one table also lists issuance of the Purchase Order as T. Hardware delivery is due T + 8 Weeks.
Risk: Support hours conflict. On-site support is stated as 24x7 in one clause and as 9 X 5 in another.

Risk: Termination notice conflicts: 90 days for failure on performance assessment in one clause, two months' notice for non-performance in another; LIC may also blacklist the vendor and levy a lump sum penalty within the limits of PBG.

Risk: The EMD Bank Guarantee format (Annexure-VI) guarantees Rs.20,00,000/- in one clause but Rs.83,00,000/- elsewhere, and sets validity at one year from BG submission, whereas the tender says one year from the last date of bid submission.
Risk: A delay beyond four (4) consecutive weeks in any phase lets LIC cancel the purchase order, levy penalties, recover from bank guarantees and terminate the contract.

overview.text: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), Department of Information Technology, Mumbai, invites e-bids for supply of Red Hat JBoss Enterprise Application Platform (EAP) and Extended Life Support (ELS) subscriptions for 1 year, to upgrade from JBoss 5, which went out of support in 2019. Bids are submitted online in two parts, Technical and Commercial. Tender Reference No. NB. HO. DIT/91165/DIT-14-20 dated 22nd September 2025.

summary.issuing_organization: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD); Department of Information Technology, Bandra Kurla Complex, Mumbai - 400051; Tender Reference No. NB. HO. DIT/91165/DIT-14-20 dated 22nd September 2025; contact Shri Anuj Bagaria, Assistant Manager

scope.text: Supply Red Hat JBoss EAP and EAP Extended Life Support (ELS) support subscriptions for one year, and provide Red Hat support services as and when required under the subscribed plan.
Quantity is 2 of each of four products: EAP 16-Core Premium (MW0153748), EAP ELS Program 16-Core Premium (MW2132048), EAP 16-Core Standard (MW0196814), EAP ELS Program 16-Core Standard (MW2122821).
Supply the subscriptions within 48 hours from the date of issue of the contract or purchase order.
Provide access to Red Hat support services, including upgrades, updates, patches and technical assistance as per the subscribed plan.
Assist in activation and configuration of JBoss EAP and ELS support on the Bank's infrastructure, and provide documentation and support for compliance and auditing.
Coordinate with the Red Hat support team to resolve issues raised by the Bank, and give timely renewal notifications and assistance for subscription continuity.
Deliverables: valid support subscription, access credentials and documentation for Red Hat support services, technical support and issue resolution, and compliance and audit documentation.
Provide contact details for support and escalation; support requests are handled under the SLA defined in the subscription plan.

key_requirements.text: Bidder must submit a letter from the OEM on its letterhead certifying the bidder is an authorised partner/SI for the JBoss EAP and ELS subscriptions. Not required if the OEM bids directly.
Bidder must submit EMD of ₹2,76,000/- (or bank guarantee); offers made without EMD will be rejected. MSEs with a valid Udyam Certificate are exempt.

Bidder must submit the Non-Blacklisting/Non-Debarment Declaration (Annexure-III), Bidder Details with seal and signature (Annexure-IV), and the Pre-Contract Integrity Pact on ₹500 stamp paper (Annexure-V).
Bidder must disclose brief litigation or dispute details on company letterhead; adverse litigation could result in disqualification at the Bank's sole discretion.
Prices must remain firm and valid for the entire contract period (one year); no price escalation will be entertained. Terms in the commercial bid format must be accepted.
The successful bidder (technically qualified L1) must submit KYC form/CKYC number and sign the SLA (Annexure-VIII) and NDA (Annexure-VI) after award of contract.
All subscriptions must be valid for the duration specified in the purchase order.

Rates quoted apply for one year from PO date for additional procurement. Additional subscriptions are bought pro-rata from delivery date, share the initial expiry date, and must be supplied within 48 hours of the PO.

Service provider must permit audit by NABARD, RBI or regulators and keep electronic books and operating records for 7 (seven) years after expiry or termination. NABARD audits need 5 business days' prior written notice.
Sub-contracting is allowed only with NABARD's prior written permission, and the service provider remains responsible for performance.

eligibility.text: Bidder must be a company registered in India under the Companies Act 1956/2013, or a partnership firm or LLP under the LLP Act 2008, with average annual turnover of ₹ 30 Lakhs for the last three FYs (2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25).

Bidder must provide PAN and GST numbers. Audited financial statements for FY 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 must be submitted to compute turnover. MSEs claim turnover exemption with a valid Udyam Certificate.

Bidder must have operating profit in at least two of the last three audited financial years (2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25). MSEs are exempt from the profitability criteria with a valid Udyam Certificate.

Net worth must be positive as at the end of the 31 March 2025 based on audited statements. A CA certificate showing turnover, profit after tax and net worth for the last three audited years is required.

Bidder must have minimum 3 years of experience supplying Red Hat Support Subscriptions to government or large private organisations, with at least three similar contracts in the last 3 years. MSEs are exempt from the experience criteria.
Bidder must provide at least 3 purchase orders from previous clients, issued in 2022-23, 2023-24 or 2024-25.
Bidder (other than OEM) must be an authorised reseller/partner/business associate of Red Hat, authorised for supply of Red Hat Support Subscriptions, and submit the OEM authorisation letter.
Bidder must not be debarred/blacklisted since 01.04.2021 by any bank, financial institution or State/Central Government, and must submit the declaration in Annexure-III.

project_duration.text: Subscription services valid for one year from the date of activation, unless otherwise specified in the purchase order.

important_conditions.text: Evaluation: Technical bids are evaluated on responses to the scope of work and the Annexure-I format; only technically qualified bidders go to commercial evaluation, where L1 is the first ranked bidder. No scoring weights or minimum technical score are specified.
Evaluation: NABARD may seek clarifications; if satisfactory clarifications are not received within the stipulated time, the respective technical parameters are treated as non-compliant.

Submission: Non-submission of any listed document, or submission with partial information, makes the bid liable for rejection.
Submission: Annexure-III declaration must also state the bidder has not withdrawn any bid after being selected as L1; a false declaration lets NABARD reject the bid or terminate the contract.

Risk: Conflicting delay penalties: SLA says 0.5% per week up to 10% of unperformed services, Schedule-A says Rs 50/- per day per product up to 10% of order value, and the payment clause refers only to penalties as per SLA (if any).

Average annual turnover of at least Rs. 30.00 Lakhs in the last 3 years in similar contracts ending 31.03.2025, shown by audited CA certified Profit & Loss statements for 2022-2023, 2023-24 & 2024-25.
Self-declaration that the bidder has not been declared ineligible or blacklisted for corrupt, fraudulent or unethical practice by any Public Organization.

overview.text: State Bank of India, Administrative Office Bhubaneswar, on behalf of CGM Bhubaneswar Circle, invites two-bid tenders on the GeM portal for an empanelment and rate contract for supply, installation, commissioning and maintenance of Biometric Access Control Systems (BACS), plus comprehensive AMC of existing BACS, at its offices in Odisha. Period is 2 +1 years. Tender ID AO BBSR: AO/BHU/SEC/2025-26/04, dated 13.01.2026.

summary.issuing_organization: State Bank of India (SBI), Administrative Office, Bhubaneswar, on behalf of CGM Bhubaneswar Circle; Assistant General Manager (Operations); Tender ID AO BBSR: AO/BHU/SEC/2025-26/04 dated 13.01.2026; agmops.bhu@sbi.co.in

scope.text: Comprehensive AMC (including ancillary work) of existing BACS, as is-where-is, at locations in Clause 2.0 of the GCC, on the draft AMC at Annexure 'H'.
Supply, installation and commissioning (including ancillary work) of new BACS with their maintenance, as per Bank work order at any location in Clause 2.0 of the GCC; rate contract for the items.
Coverage is approx. 235 branches, offices and establishments under AO Bhubaneswar; BACS is presently installed at 05 (Five) currency chest branches.
Mandatory AMC visit once every month to each currency chest branch, that is 12 (twelve) visits a year, with a minimum gap of 20 days between visits.

AMC covers replacement of faulty switches, sensors, testing push buttons, indicators and power supply module; it excludes replacing the entire BACS panel, rewiring, and damage from lightening, arson, fire or flooding.
Integration or compatibility with the Central Monitoring Station may be required; the station is under development and the bidder must give an undertaking at Annexure 'D'.
If BACS is later installed at non-currency chest branches, they are covered under the same agreement, rates and terms; visit frequency is decided by the Bank.
Submit a Quarterly AMC report with time-wise breakdown by email in Excel format and as hard copy to the AGM (Ops), AO Bhubaneswar.

key_requirements.text: Biometric reader (Annexure 'A'): fingerprint type with 32bit processor, 500 DPI optical sensor, storage up to 1000 fingerprints, identification in less than or equal to about 1 sec, FAR (False Rejection) 0.1 % or less.
Magnetic lock (Annexure 'A'): holding force 1200 lbs, current drain 300mA at 12VDC, power-off to open, adjustable relock delay 0.5 to 30 seconds; certifications UL & CE.
Annexure 'A' specifications are minimum; bidders may quote equivalent or higher specifications, but no weight is given for higher configurations.
Vendor must guarantee 100% system uptime for the full equipment configuration in every quarter.
Complaints must be attended until resolved within 24 hours for Urban/Metro, 36 hours for Semi Urban and 48 hours for Rural locations; Difficult Centre limits are decided by the Circle.
Vendor must hold a technical support SLA with the OEM for 05 years, in effect for the contract period, with undertaking at Annexure 'E'.
Only original or new materials from the OEM may be used; no refurbished, second hand or spurious materials; ISI-marked products where no make is specified.
Technician must carry enough spares such as sensors, switches, power supply module and wires to replace parts during the AMC visit itself.
Vendor must obtain a police verification report of its staff before engaging them to work in branches.
Vendor must not employ any person who is not an Indian National.

eligibility.text: Must have minimum 07 years (Seven Years) of experience in supply, installation, testing, commissioning and maintenance of BACS, as one entity, with Government/PSU (at least One) and Public Sector Banks (at least three); work orders to be submitted.
Must have average annual turnover of Rs. 3000/- for each year in the last 3 years as one entity ending on 31st March 2025.
Must provide a solvency certificate of Rs. 3000/ - from any scheduled Bank, not older than three months from the date of tender.

Similar completed works required: three works of not less than 40% of estimated cost (Rs. 4000/- each), two works of 50% (Rs. 5000/- each) and one work of 80% (Rs. 8000/-); the document lists these as separate rows without stating they are alternatives.

Must have installed BACS in each of FY 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25, 20 Numbers per year, in Government/PSU (at least One) and Public Sector Banks (at least three), with work orders and completion certificates.
Must have AMC of minimum 25 BACS in three years each (Minimum 20 BACS AMC per year) for 2022-23, 2023-24 & 2024-25, with work orders and completion certificates.

Must declare it is not on any Caution list of RBI / IBA, not blacklisted by any Bank / PSU / Government department, and has no pending litigation with any Bank / PSU / Government (details to be given if yes).
Registered office/service centre in the State of Odisha is preferred, or the bidder must be ready to open one within 45 days after issuing of work order.

important_dates.text: Tender dated 13.01.2026.

Bid submission deadline: Not specified in the document; bids are due on or before the last date of submission shown on the GeM Portal.
Query deadline: date not specified in the document; queries received after the scheduled date and time are not responded to.
Technical bid opening is as per the dates on the GeM Portal; if that day is a holiday, bids open on the next working day.
Bid validity: 180 days from the date of opening of price bid.
Experience in Annexure F is counted over the last Seven Years effective from 30th November 2025.

commercial_requirements.text: EMD Rs. 100/- as demand draft in favour of "Assistant General Manager (Operations), AO, Bhubaneswar" payable at Bhubaneswar (the NIT summary says in favour of "SBI"); exempted for Micro and Small Enterprises with valid MSME/UDYAM certificate.

Additional Security Deposit/Additional Performance Guarantee applies if the bid price is below 10% of the estimated cost; amount is the difference between 90% of estimated cost and the quoted price; bank guarantee or FDR accepted.
Performance guarantee of 10% of the contract value from a Scheduled Commercial Bank other than State Bank of India, in the Bank's format (draft SLA, Annexure 'H').
No advance payment and no part payment; AMC charges are paid quarterly in arrears after deducting penalties; payment by electronic fund transfer.

Rate firm and inclusive of all costs, taxes, levies but excluding GST, which is paid separately on invoice.
Delay in work beyond the stipulated period attracts penalty of minimum 0.5% to maximum 05% per week, not exceeding 05% of estimated work/contract value.

AMC SLA penalties come off the quarterly payment: uptime below 100.00% costs 1% to 6% of that quarter's AMC amount by band and 20% below 95%; Rs. 100/- per day of late complaint resolution; Rs. 500/- per week of delayed AMC.

project_duration.text: Rate contract valid for 02 years + 01 years from award, subject to yearly review; Bank may at its sole discretion extend up to 01 Year on existing rate and terms.
New equipment carries warranty for 02 years from installation; comprehensive AMC applies from the 3rd year onward for 03 years.

Evaluation: Work is allotted to the L1 bidder through the GeM algorithm; L1 must communicate written acceptance within the stipulated time on GEM or its bid is cancelled.

Submission: Missing any one document listed in the Bid Evaluation Criteria leads to rejection of the technical bid; tenders on any format other than the prescribed one are summarily rejected.
Submission: Enclose Annexure F response sheet, Annexure 'D' and 'E' on letter head, GST filing copies for September 2025, October 2025 and November 2025, and Annexure 'H' signed on all pages.
Submission: Queries go through the pre-bid meeting or in writing on GeM portal only; no other mode of communication is entertained.

Risk: Contract period conflicts: 02 years + 01 years in the NIT and GCC against one year renewable yearly to a total of three years in the BEC; warranty is Two Year in the GCC against Five year with rates valid for 05 years in the BOQ notes.
Risk: Liability is uncapped: vendor indemnifies the Bank on first demand and the Bank may claim damages without any limitation.

overview.text: The Superintending Archaeologist, Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), Hampi Circle, Hosapete, Karnataka, on behalf of the President of India, invites online two-cover tenders for Development Works to Mahadeva Temple (Construction of Visitor Amenities and Sculpture Shed) at Itagi for the year 2025-26. Estimated cost is Rs. 78,14,000.00 and the work completion period is 180 days. Reference No: Sout/Hamp/Kopa/Maha/23179449.

summary.issuing_organization: Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), Ministry of Culture, Government of India; Hampi Circle, Hosapete, through the Superintending Archaeologist (Tender Inviting Authority), for the President of India; Tender ID Sout/Hamp/Kopa/Maha/23179449; Ref D-42/15/2026-Hampi Circle; sahc.asi@gov.in

scope.text: Construct a boundary/compound wall with grill and gates around the site, a sculpture shed for exhibiting/storing sculptures, and other associated works at Mahadeva Temple, Itagi.
Associated ground works include clearing and grubbing road, earthwork excavation, laterite stone kerb, heavy duty cobble stones 75mm thick, and signage posts for direction and place identification.
Schedule of quantities covers masonry, concrete, steel and stone work, e.g. earth work excavation 285.15 Cum, random rubble masonry in foundation 136.41 Cum, coursed rubble masonry 83.94 Cum.
Fix MS grill on top of the boundary wall, 8605.0 Kg, to a height of 1.30 mtrs, and MS gates at 5 locations, 2230 Kg.
Sculpture shed: structural steel work 2465 Kg and 1260 Kg, and corrugated G.I. sheet roofing 73.95 Sqm and 37.80 Sqm.
Granite stone flooring 301.6 Sqm and 10 granite stone benches.
Demolish stone rubble masonry 17.49 Cum, dispose debris 59.4 Cum, and shift artifacts/stone members from inside to the sculpture shed (100 Cum).
Actual quantities may vary higher or lower than tendered quantities; the sub circle in-charge or site in-charge decides the actual quantity.

key_requirements.text: Bid must include the Bid Securing Declaration (Form 8); a bid without it is rejected as nonresponsive.
Bid must quote the entire works in the schedule; conditional, alternative or multiple bids are rejected as nonresponsive.
Bidder must sign and submit the Integrity Pact (Form 9) with the tender; bidders who do not are disqualified.
Downloaded tender documents must not be altered while uploading, except filling required information; otherwise the bid is rejected.
Work must be completed as per approved design and specifications, free from defects, and within the stipulated timeline.
Materials must be of high quality and conform to relevant Indian Standards, and entirely new and unused; the successful bidder must produce a sample of materials to match the monument.
Contractor must take utmost care that no damage is caused to the monument; the site is a non-smoking and non-plastic area and the agency must strictly comply.
Sub-contracting, transfer, assignment or pledging of rights and liabilities under the contract is not allowed.
Contractor must hold a valid licence under the Contract Labour (R&A) Act, 1970 before starting work, and only labourers aged between eighteen to sixty years may be engaged.
Price schedule (Excel) must be filled with non-zero rates and no blank cells; prices must be in Indian Rupees only, with GST shown separately.

eligibility.text: Must be a contractor or company registered with ASI / CPWD / PWD / MES / Local Bodies and have experience in conservation or civil works in heritage monuments/buildings; Ltd / Pvt Ltd companies must also be registered under the Companies Act,1956. JV Consortium is not permitted.

Must not be insolvent, bankrupt or wound up, nor blacklisted/banned/debarred by ASI or Government of India agencies, nor convicted within three years preceding the last date of bid submission for the specified offences.
Must not be associated with a retired Gazetted officer within the one year cooling-off period, or with near relations of ASI executives involved in this tender, and must have no conflict of interest.

Must provide a Statutory Auditor certificate (Annexure 4) for FY 2022-23, FY 2023-24 & FY 2024-25 showing average annual turnover of at least 30% of the estimated amount, plus Income Tax Returns for the same three years.

Experience in the last seven years: must show either three similar completed works each not less than 40 % of the estimated cost, or two each not less than 50 %, or one not less than 80% of the estimated cost.

Similar work means any kind of conservation works / civil works in heritage monuments/buildings under Central / State Department; proof is the work order plus a completion certificate stating value and duration.

Must provide valid GST registration with returns/challans of last four quarters of FY 2024-25, PAN card, and EPF and ESIC registration with ECRs of last four quarters of FY 2024-25; labour department registration is listed as desirable ('should be registered').
Bidder must declare it has not been blacklisted or debarred by any Government of India Ministry/Department in the last three (3) Years and has actually seen the work site.

EMD Rs. 1,96,000.00 by demand draft payable at Hosapete in favour of the Superintending Archaeologist, ASI Hampi Circle; original must reach by 10.02.2026 at 15.00 Hrs; DD valid only if drawn during the NIT notice period; offers without EMD are rejected.

Performance security of 5% of the Contract / awarded value, as DD / FDR / banker's cheque or bank guarantee from a commercial bank in India, must be furnished within fourteen days of the Letter of Award and stay valid till completion of obligations.

project_duration.text: Work completion period is 180 days.

Bidder must not be presently banned, delisted, blacklisted or debarred by Central Government, State Government, Union Territory, PSU or Government Department; undertaking in Format-F/03.
In the last Five (5) years the bidder must not have failed to perform on any agreement, been expelled from a project, or had an agreement terminated for breach; undertaking in Format-F/04.
Bidder must have at least 50 full time employees in its consulting division/business unit on payroll; undertaking in Format-F/07.
Bidder must have experience of over 5 years of consultancy services in the Indian power sector, with at least one contract awarded prior to 01.04.2017; documents in Format-F/08.

Average minimum annual turnover of INR 50 Crores during each of FY 2019-20, FY 2020-21 and FY 2021-22 from consulting/advisory business in India (Format-F/05), and positive net worth in each of those years (Format-F/06).

Bidder must have successfully completed at least two (2) retainership engagements of not less than 1 year, each of minimum value INR 20 lacs in last 5 years (after 01.04.2018), giving project management support to Central/State govt agencies; milestone or deliverable-based work does not qualify; Format-F/09.

overview.text: Maharashtra State Electricity Transmission Co. Ltd. (MSETCL) invites proposals to select a Project Management Consultant for implementation of a Corporate Level Data Warehouse for MSETCL. Selection is a two-stage Quality and Cost Based process with separate technical and financial envelopes. The Terms of Reference (Schedule-1) with scope and contract duration are not included in the document.

summary.issuing_organization: Maharashtra State Electricity Transmission Co. Ltd. (MSETCL), Government of Maharashtra; Office of the Chief Engineer (Contracts & Monitoring), Plot No. C-19, E-Block, Prakashganga, BKC, Bandra (E), Mumbai-51; RFP notice number left blank; Tel 022-2659 8589; cecm@mahatransco.in

scope.text: Select a Project Management Consultant who will prepare the deliverables for implementation of the Corporate Level Data Warehouse Project for MSETCL.
Detailed objectives, services and deliverables are in the Terms of Reference (Schedule-1), which is not included in the document.
Data Analytic Consultant/Expert (key personnel) is responsible for overall progress and completion of the project and leads the entire project team.
Domain Analytic Consultant/Expert (key personnel) is responsible for project implementation and monitoring and for power sector domain suggestions including relevant analytical tools.
Other competent Professional Personnel must be added as required to complete the consultancy within the time schedule; a CV for each must be submitted in the Annexure-II format.
After the report is accepted, the Authority may require Key Personnel and Professional Personnel to visit the Project or its offices for further consultations or desk work.

key_requirements.text: Proposal is considered responsive only if it is on the Annexure I form, received by the due date, has the Bid Security and Power of Attorney, is signed, sealed, hard-bound, complete, and has no conditions.
Any bid not accompanied by the Bid Security will be rejected as non-responsive.
Technical Proposal must not include any information relating to the price quoted.
Financial Proposal must include all costs and taxes, with no condition or assumption attached; otherwise it is non-responsive and liable to be rejected.
Total cost (Item G of Annexure-X) must be stated in Indian Rupees in figures and words; if they differ, the words prevail, and if the arithmetic total differs, the lower of the two prevails.
Rates quoted must be firm until the Authority accepts the deliverables and all Consultant obligations under the Agreement are discharged.
One CV per Key Personnel position, no alternatives; CVs must be recently signed and dated in blue ink and countersigned by the Applicant; photocopied or unsigned CVs will be rejected.
No Key Personnel may have attained the age of 75 (seventy five) years at the time of submitting the proposal.
Each Key Personnel CV must be a minimum of 4 pages and a maximum of 8 pages and must not be older than three months from the date of submission.
Annexure IX methodology: understanding of TOR not more than two pages and methodology and work plan not more than three pages; marks are deducted for lengthy or out-of-context responses.

eligibility.text: Applicant must have completed at least three major projects in Data Warehousing, preferably in the power sector or an equivalent field, in the past five years, with documentary evidence and work completion certificate.
Applicant must have a development/support centre in India to support the project at any given point of time during execution.

Key personnel: Data Analytic expert (B.Tech/M.Tech in IT, Electronics or Computer Science, with large data acquisition and analytics project experience in past three years) and Domain Analytic expert (B.Tech/M.Tech in Electrical Engineering, at least 10 years in transmission projects, O&M or automation).

Minimum turnover must be twice the offered bid price, proved by a statutory auditor or Chartered Accountant certificate; earlier years are enhanced by factors 1.00 (2016-17), 1.05 (2015-16) and 1.10 (2014-15).
Applicant must submit audited financial reports for the last three years, and the latest valid Income Tax and GST certificates and registration certificate.
An entity barred by the Central Government, a State Government, a statutory authority or a public sector undertaking, with the bar subsisting on the proposal date, is not eligible.

In the last three years the Applicant or its Associate must not have failed to perform on any agreement (penalty by arbitral or judicial authority), been expelled from a project, or had an agreement terminated for breach.
Applicant may bid alone or as lead member of a consortium; JV projects count by JV share and projects done as an associate get 25% weightage.

important_dates.text: Downloading of revised application documents: from 26.10.2017.

commercial_requirements.text: RFP fee Rs. 5000/+ GST as applicable, non-refundable; if downloaded, the fee must still be deposited (cash, DD or Pay order) with the physical submission, and an application without proof of fee will not be considered.
EMD of Rs. 1 lakh as token bid security, as Bank Guarantee (Annexure-VI) of a nationalized or scheduled bank valid for 3 years from the due date of submission.

Bid Security is interest free and is forfeited for a non-responsive proposal, prohibited practices, withdrawal during validity, failure to reconfirm at negotiation, failure to sign the Agreement or start the assignment, or conflict of interest.
Selected consultancy must submit a bank guarantee (Annexure-VI) and other documents for the agreement; amount and validity are not stated, and delay in submission retains payment.
Price basis: Indian Rupees, all costs and taxes deemed included, payments subject to deduction of taxes at source.
No escalation on any account is payable on the Annexure-X amounts.
Miscellaneous Expenses in Item A VIII shall not exceed 15% (fifteen per cent) of the total amount in Item D.
Not specified in the document: payment terms and milestones, liquidated damages and penalties, performance security amount, warranty

project_duration.text: Not specified in the document: contract duration, extension terms and delivery milestones are in the Terms of Reference, which is not included.
Selected Applicant must sign and return the duplicate copy of the Letter of Award within 7 (seven) days of receiving it.
Consultant must commence services at the Project site within 7 (seven) days of the date of the Agreement or another mutually agreed date.

important_conditions.text: Evaluation: Two-stage Quality and Cost Based Selection; technical evaluation first, financial evaluation only of shortlisted applicants, ranking on combined score, and the highest-ranked applicant is invited for negotiation.
Evaluation: Technical marks: experience 20 points, work plan and methodology 20 points, key staff 30 points (Data Analytic 15, Domain analytic 15), presentation and discussion 30 points.
Evaluation: Minimum qualifying technical score is 75 points; weights are Technical Proposal 0.70 and Financial Proposal 0.30; S = St x T% + Sf x P%.
Evaluation: Not more than five applicants are shortlisted for financial evaluation; on equal total score the higher technical score wins.
Submission: Hard-bound form only with serially numbered pages and an index, each page initialed; one original plus one soft copy and one hard copy marked COPY.
Submission: Sealed outer envelope containing two sealed envelopes, Technical Proposal (Annexure I, Annexures II to X, supporting documents, Bid Security) and Financial Proposal.
Submission: Physical delivery on or before the Proposal Due Date time; proposals by fax, telex, telegram or e-mail are not entertained.
Submission: Annexure V undertaking on non-debarment, blacklisting and litigation, and Annexure VII Power of Attorney on non-judicial stamp paper of Rs. 100 (one hundred), notarized.
Risk: Conflict on query response timing: 11 days prior to the Proposal Due Date in the schedule versus not later than 7 (seven) days prior in the clarification clause.
Risk: Bid Security validity conflict: 3 years from the due date in the clause versus 1 year in the Annexure-VI format, which also refers to a forest-land clearance consultancy.
Risk: All schedule dates are in 2017 (Proposal Due Date 09.11.2017); whether this RFP is still open is not stated.
Risk: Terms of Reference (Schedule-1) with the objectives, scope of services and deliverables are not attached; duration and payment terms are also not given.
Risk: Indemnity of up to 3 (three) times the value of the Agreement for any direct loss or damage caused by deficiency in services.

Risk: Key Personnel substitution only for incapacity or health, with 20% deduction from their remuneration on first and 50% on second substitution; false averment by Key Personnel can lead to 5 (five) years debarment.

overview.text: Southern California Public Power Authority (SCPPA), on behalf of its Member utilities, solicits proposals for renewable energy projects or products, optionally with co-located energy storage, for commercial operation or delivery starting in 2025 and beyond. Structures may be SCPPA ownership or a power purchase agreement with or without an ownership option. Rolling RFP issued February 14, 2025; proposals due June 30, 2025.

summary.issuing_organization: Southern California Public Power Authority (SCPPA), acting for its Member utilities; Q1/Q2 2025 Renewable Energy Resources and Energy Storage Solutions RFP; contact renewablesrfp@scppa.org; reference number not specified in the document

scope.text: Renewable energy projects or products under the California RPS programs, with commercial operation or delivery starting in 2025 and beyond.
Accepted structures: SCPPA project ownership, a PPA with an ownership option, or a PPA without an ownership option.

Eligible resources include wind, geothermal, biomass, biomethane, hydro, solar, solar thermal, waste-to-energy, renewable fuel cells, permanent load shifting, hydrogen, flexible and hybrid projects, and unbundled RECs.
Energy storage may be proposed only combined with a renewable energy project.
Portfolio Content Category 2 and 3 REC-only proposals are also considered, for any term.
Delivery term: minimum is 1 month with no maximum; both short-term and long-term (greater than 10 years) delivery sought.
Delivery at the listed points of delivery (CAISO Grid with preference of SP15, among others) or other points if all transmission, ancillary and scheduling costs are included.
Out of scope: stand-alone energy storage, to be proposed under SCPPA's separate Standalone Energy Storage RFP.

key_requirements.text: Proposal must be signed by an officer authorized to bind the Respondent, with the non-collusion declaration in the transmittal letter.
Only proven renewable technologies; experimental or speculative proposals will not be entertained.
Facility must be RPS compliant and compliant with the California Energy Commission emissions performance standard (EPS) upon COD and throughout the term.
Seller must assume the risk of bringing the facility back into RPS or EPS compliance if a change in law makes it noncompliant.
Energy storage paired with a renewable project must have capacity of at least one half the total interconnection capacity offered and a duration of at least 4 hours.
Respondent must handle site control (SCPPA must be allowed to assume or cure any default in site control documents) and bears environmental liability, hazardous materials and removal.
Respondent must obtain all construction, operational and environmental permits and licenses, and construction financing.
SCPPA must receive all environmental attributes and all capacity rights associated with the project.
Project must be certified RPS-eligible by the California Energy Commission no later than 6 months after COD and registered in WREGIS no later than 3 months before COD.
If a SCPPA Member is in the EIM, acceptance into the Energy Imbalance Market is required before any test energy; Seller must give technical design data at least nine months before test energy.

eligibility.text: Minimum turnover, years of experience, number of similar projects and certifications: Not specified in the document

Must provide current financial statements of all entities involved: audited statements not more than twelve months old, annual reports, FERC Form 1; otherwise verifiable statements for the past three (3) years and Dun & Bradstreet number where available.
Must identify project participants and key personnel with their qualifications and experience on similar projects, and give a commitment statement for retaining them.
Must list existing projects in commercial operation and references for similar completed projects, with contact person, phone number and address.
Must disclose any service rendered to SCPPA or its Members within the last five (5) years, or else give references over that period.
Must address possible conflicts of interest with SCPPA and Members, including lawsuits; these do not automatically disqualify.
Must indicate all pending litigation that could affect the proposal, existing contracts, operation or financial stability.
Must not offer gifts or promises of remuneration to SCPPA or Member officials or staff, and must not collude with other respondents.

important_dates.text: RFP issued February 14, 2025; RFP open period February 14, 2025-June 30, 2025 (rolling RFP).
Clarification questions due June 20, 2025.
Responses to clarification questions: 5 Business Days after submitted.
Proposals due on or before 12:00 PM PPT on June 30, 2025.
Review of proposals: 5 Business Days after submittal, during the RFP open period.
Interviews (if necessary): TBD.
Selection of Respondent(s): from submittal date to no later than June 30, 2025.
Proposal validity: twelve (12) months from the Proposals Due date, unless the Respondent states a shorter term.
Bid opening date: Not specified in the document

commercial_requirements.text: Fixed energy price (preferred): nominal $/MWh as of the year of COD, no escalation, covering energy, capacity, RECs and all other products.
Alternative: variable index energy price plus fixed capacity/REC price in nominal $/MWh with no escalation; preferred by some Member utilities.
Storage price must be quoted in addition to the energy price, in $/MWh and in $/kW-month for a minimum of 4-hour systems; include a Solar-Only price if solar and BESS are proposed.
Any price increase after proposal submittal could end negotiations and prompt reevaluation of the proposal.
Transmission cost to the delivery point must be in the energy price; CAISO delivery must include a $/MWh price adder fixed for the contract term.
Ownership offer must state a purchase price at COD in $/kW plus recurring owner costs; PPA with purchase option must give a buyout price or formula and an energy price without buyout.
Performance Assurance amounts in nominal dollars must be stated, through COD and after COD as a Letter of Credit; SCPPA may require performance security before negotiations.
Not specified in the document: EMD or bid security, tender fee, payment terms, liquidated damages and warranty

project_duration.text: Delivery term: minimum of 1 month with no maximum; PPA terms up to the life of the facility will be considered.
Contract duration and award date: Not specified in the document
Respondent must propose COD and a major milestone schedule through construction, test energy and COD.

important_conditions.text: Evaluation: initial screening eliminates proposals that are non-responsive, miss minimum requirements, are not economically competitive, or come from Respondents lacking creditworthiness or financial resources.
Evaluation: each Member Agency applies its own criteria, which may include price, size, location, schedule, COD, viability, guarantees and fit with its resource plan.
Evaluation: scoring weights and minimum score: Not specified in the document
Evaluation: project evaluations include the full cost of delivery to customers of Member Agencies in Southern California.
Submission: one electronic copy must be emailed to renewablesrfp@scppa.org by 12:00PM (PPT) on June 30, 2025; one hard copy is optional, to Glendora, California.

Submission: proposal must include all Section V required elements (transmittal letter, respondent information, renewable category, project details, experience, references, conflicts); SCPPA may disqualify one that does not.
Submission: Term Sheet (Appendix A) must be completed, and the ESS Specifications (Appendix B) for storage within LADWP's Balancing Authority; both are posted as separate documents.
Submission: must identify proprietary material exempt from the Public Records Act, or exemption is waived.
Risk: SCPPA may award irrespective of price or technical ability, reject all proposals for any reason, and proposers have no legal recourse.
Risk: schedule is subject to change, interviews are TBD, and SCPPA may start negotiations and sign agreements before the proposal deadline.
Risk: Seller bears the risk of RPS or EPS noncompliance from a change in law for the PPA term.
Risk: all contact with SCPPA Board, staff or Members on this RFP, outside the specified method, is prohibited until contract execution and may mean immediate disqualification.
Risk: CEQA compliance is required before SCPPA can execute an agreement, and test energy before COD is curtailable at any time without compensation.
Risk: listing protectable documents obliges the Respondent to indemnify and defend SCPPA against disclosure claims.

overview.text: Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited (SECI), on behalf of MNRE, invites proposals from an agency to establish a Programme Management Unit supporting the National Mission on Cleantech Manufacturing. The engagement is for an initial period of two (2) years, extendable by one (1) year at the discretion of SECI/MNRE. Ref. SECI/C&P/MI/00/05/26-27 dated 15.09.2026.

summary.issuing_organization: Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited (A Government of India Enterprise, under MNRE); Contracts & Procurement, 6th Floor, Plate-B, NBCC Office Block Tower-2, East Kidwai Nagar, New Delhi - 110023; Ref. SECI/C&P/MI/00/05/26-27 dated 15.09.2026; contracts@seci.co.in

scope.text: Establish a PMU to support MNRE on the National Mission on Cleantech Manufacturing across solar, wind, green hydrogen and energy storage, plus other cleantech manufacturing sectors such as EVs and advanced batteries, very high voltage transmission equipment and waste to energy.
Work is structured as two integrated work packages: strategy, indigenization and ecosystem (Work Package 1) and states strategy, investment mobilization and implementation (Work Package 2).

Work Package 1: value chain reports for solar, wind, green hydrogen and energy storage; benchmarking against at least five peer economies; sector indigenization strategies with year-wise localization targets till 2030.
Work Package 1 also covers policy and investment frameworks, editable sector financial models, R&D and skilling roadmaps, and stakeholder consultations (at least 10 per sector).

Work Package 2: state-wise manufacturing upscaling strategy identifying 15 States/UTs, manufacturing cluster facilitation plans, investment pipeline tracker, circular economy and raw material strategy, and state ease-of-doing-business support.
Work Package 2 also covers a KPI-linked results framework, a consolidated report on cleantech manufacturing in India, state handholding, and any other related assignments directed by MNRE.

Additional scope: monthly price trend and forecasting reports, carbon credit pricing and market intelligence module, policy updates, quarterly deep-dive assessments, ad-hoc alerts within 72 hours and an annual outlook with three-year projections.
Agency may also be required to provide back-end support as directed by MNRE.

key_requirements.text: Must deploy a seven-post team: Team Leader/Program Manager, four Cleantech Sector Specialists (Solar, Wind, Green Hydrogen, Energy Storage), Policy, Investment & Workforce Expert and Program Associate.

Minimum experience: Team Leader 10 Years; each Sector Specialist and the Policy, Investment & Workforce Expert 5 years; Program Associate 2 years. Master's degree required for the senior posts, Bachelor's degree for Program Associate.
Team must be stationed at MNRE full-time for the contract period; MNRE provides seating, the Agency arranges laptops etc.
Must submit a list of deployed resources within seven days of Work Order issuance; MNRE may interview them and may seek replacement of any resource at any time.
Must share a declaration that deployed manpower is independent and not working on any other project, and an NDA for data privacy and data security.
Any replacement resource must have the same or higher qualifications and experience, to MNRE's satisfaction, at no additional price.
Must submit reports to MNRE with a copy to SECI: Monthly Comprehensive Market Report, Quarterly Deep-Dive Report, Ad-hoc Alerts within 72 hours of impactful developments, and Annual Outlook Report.
Deliverables are examined by an MNRE Screening Committee on alignment with scope, quality, methodology, timeliness and presence of the committed manpower at MNRE.

Additional manpower (maximum up to five personnel) must be provided on MNRE approval at the same rates, with monthly rates derived from Y = Z/30 (Program Associate Y/15; specialists (2*Y)/15; Program Manager (4*Y)/15).
Agency is solely responsible for employment, remuneration and statutory and labour law compliance for deployed personnel.

eligibility.text: Applicant must be a Company; registered LLP, Partnership Firm or Sole Proprietorship Firm are also eligible. Bids must come from a single legal entity.
Consortium or joint venture not eligible; Trusts, NGOs and Educational Societies not eligible.
Selected Agency must not engage any other external agency, NGO or third party for PMU delivery (except individual experts or staff employed directly), and must not use external funding or grants.

Must not be barred, debarred or blacklisted by Central/State Government, a PSU, MNRE or SECI; must not be under liquidation or receivership on the bid due date; no failure to perform, penalty, expulsion or termination in the last 3 (three) years. Undertaking required.

Must have been in the field of similar works for not less than 03 Years as on last date of bid submission. Similar Works means large scale assistance programs covering strategy and Governance, Policy formulation/knowledge partnership services.

Must have completed one similar work order of INR 4,88,00,000 or more, or two of INR 3,05,00,000 or more, or three of INR 2,44,00,000 or more, in the last three years. Ongoing contracts count if executed for at least one (1) year with a satisfactory client certificate.
Minimum Average Annual Turnover of INR 2,44,00,000 over FY 2023-24, 2024-25 & 2025-26; net worth for the last financial year must be positive.
Minimum Working Capital of INR 76,25,000/- per last audited statement, or a bank letter (bank net worth not less than INR 500 Crores) confirming a line of credit of at least INR 76,25,000/-.

important_dates.text: RfP issued under reference dated 15.09.2026.

Outstation travel needs prior MNRE approval; reimbursed at lower of actuals or Rs. 10,000/- one-way, Rs. 7,000/- per day for stay (80% and 60% in Y and Z class cities) and Rs. 10,000/- per trip for local journeys.

Work Package 1 duration within 12 months; first deliverables Month 1 (baseline reports), Month 2 (benchmarking, indigenization strategy, Policy Action Note), Month 4 (investment framework, R&D roadmap, skilling strategy); Consolidated WP-1 Report Month 12.

overview.text: Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC) invites e-procurement bids to appoint a consultant for surveying, digitization and geo-referencing of its immovable assets (parks, markets, shops, buildings, lands and similar) for LB Nagar Zone and Kukatpally Zone, under Notice No. RFP-01/TP/HO/GHMC/2025-26. Selection is by QCBS and the contract period is 6 Months.

summary.issuing_organization: Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation (GHMC); O/o Chief City Planner, Town Planning Section, Head Office, Tank Bund, Hyderabad; Notice No. RFP-01/TP/HO/GHMC/2025-26 dt: 09.04.2025; ccp.ghmc@gmail.com, 8897723423

scope.text: Detailed physical survey of GHMC immovable properties using DGPS to collect boundary measurements, extent, physical features, building foot prints and surrounding features.
Collect real world co-ordinates of every property corner using DGPS, and record height above MSL for each property.
Prepare detailed plans of each property at a scale of 1 : 200 to 1:1000 and capture photographs of frontage, sides and inside.
Collect property attribute details (circle, layout, extent, Sy. No., encroachment, boundaries, GPS coordinates and others) and generate a Unique ID Number for each property.
Design and develop a geo-enabled mobile application integrated with base map/Google Map for survey and attribute collection, and integrate attribute data with spatial data.
Prepare a profile of every immovable property and the Inventory of immovable properties in the prescribed format.
Develop and implement a software application to monitor the immovable properties of GHMC.
Deliverables include raw and corrected DGPS readings in RINEX and native format, maps in CAD and KML format with shape files, and the report in Hard Copy (8 Sets) plus soft copy.

key_requirements.text: Each Pre-Qualification criterion in Section 4.1 is mandatory; a bid that fails any one is non-responsive and not evaluated further.
DGPS rover readings at each property corner must have a minimum observation period of 15 minutes; RTK-DGPS is preferred.
Base stations must use Multi/Dual frequency DGPS receivers with a minimum observation time of 12 hours from the nearest SOI control point.
Base-to-rover distance must be less than 10 km for single frequency DGPS rovers and less than 50 kms for dual frequency rovers.
DGPS instruments must be set to Geographic Coordinate System WGS84 Datum.
Raw and differentially corrected DGPS readings with error charts must be submitted to the Authority every week or as soon as the work is completed, whichever is earlier.
Survey is proposed in all 6 zones simultaneously with at least 2 Teams per Zone; each Team has a Team Leader (Specialist in Geomatics), a DGPS Operator and/or ATS Operator, and surveyors.
Key personnel minimum qualifications are prescribed; the Project Manager needs B.E/B.Tech or equivalent and at least 5 years of experience, and CVs of key personnel must be enclosed.
Coordinates must be delivered in 8 decimal places in degrees for Latitude and Longitude including Height above MSL in meters.
Source Code of the customized GIS Solution must be transferred to GHMC; software licences must be genuine, perpetual and in the name of GHMC.

eligibility.text: Bidder must be a registered company, partnership firm, LLP or proprietorship firm in operation for at least 5 years.

Consortium is allowed with not more than two companies, a stamped consortium agreement and a Lead Partner; every member must be jointly and severally liable. MoU must be submitted with the Pre-Qualification Bid.

Experience in last 10 years in India: at least 2 completed Total Station and DGPS property survey projects for Government/PSU/ULB, plus at least 2 projects each for spatial layer creation and MIS-GIS integration with Web and Mobile Applications.
Cumulative turnover of at least INR 1 Crore during last five financial years as on 31 March 2024 from Property Survey and GIS Software implementation.
Bidder or Lead Partner must have positive net worth in the last financial year ending on March 2024.
Bidder must have at least 20 regular experts for Land Survey and GIS, and a local office at Hyderabad.
Bidder must not be blacklisted by any Central or State Government Department or PSU as on bid submission date, and must have a valid GST Registration in India.
Bidder must have back-end support arrangement with GIS software licence provider and IT hardware OEMs, and authorization from OEM/licence provider to quote, with Perpetual License.
